scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQUESTER-FRAMING.statement: The requester's framing is correct: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

H-ROOT-CAUSE-UNKNOWN.statement: The operational root cause differs from the requested solution and must be established from data

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation shows dispute tickets rose from ~600 per month in June‑July to ~1,200 per month in August‑September, confirming a roughly two‑fold increase since August.
The observation shows that among disputed bills, 1,785 are associated with actual reads and 1,240 with estimated reads, indicating actual reads are linked to more disputes than estimated reads.
Field route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the target of 0.95. This shortfall suggests field operations may be underperforming, potentially contributing to billing disputes.
Median dispute response time is 1.6 days with p90 at 2.8 days, within the 3‑day SLA, showing response speed is not delayed despite high ticket volume (2440 tickets).
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff modifications have been made recently; therefore tariff changes are not a source of the billing errors driving the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The shortage of three field readers since July causes routes to run late, leading to estimated bills for affected customers.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder claims there has been no tariff change this year, indicating tariff modifications are not contributing to the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes can be requested by the utility but must be executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation, showing that this protected action requires Field Ops Manager approval.

problem_definition.root_problem: Low field route completion (below target) causes delayed or missed manual meter reads, leading to inaccurate billing (via estimation or erroneous actual reads) that drives the observed doubling of dispute tickets since August.

trace.summary: Low field route completion (below target) causes delayed or missed manual meter reads, leading to inaccurate billing (via estimation or erroneous actual reads) that drives the observed doubling of dispute tickets since August.

Residual disputes may persist due to AMI read validation degradation (U-U6) and unknown split between estimation and actual read errors (U-U1); an agent could assist with ticket handling but does not address root cause.

structural_remedies.description: Increase field staffing (add three readers or overtime) to achieve target route completion, which does not violate K-DISPATCH or K-BILLWRITE [E-06, E-03, A-A3, K-DISPATCH, K-BILLWRITE].
structural_remedies.rationale: Hiring/training exceeds remaining 225 minutes.; residual gap: AMI read validation degradation (U-U6) and unknown proportion of estimation vs actual read errors (U-U1) may still cause disputes [U-U6, U-U1].

structural_remedies.description: Optimize route scheduling and prioritization using existing staff, requiring Field Operations Manager confirmation (K-DISPATCH) and respecting K-BILLWRITE [E-08, K-DISPATCH, K-BILLWRITE].
structural_remedies.rationale: Can be planned and approved within remaining time.; residual gap: Staffing shortage may limit achievable completion; AMI read issues (U-U6) remain [E-06, U-U6].

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request asserts that wrong bills are driving dispute growth and that an AI agent can fix them.

hypotheses.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August due to incorrect bill generation; an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and fixes bills will resolve the surge.
hypotheses.rationale: If billing errors are the root cause, an AI agent that can correct bills and respond to tickets would directly reduce disputes.

hypotheses.statement: Delayed or incomplete manual meter reads from the field contractor cause estimation errors, leading to inflated bills and disputes.
hypotheses.rationale: If field read delays are responsible, fixing the AI agent alone would not address the missing reads; process or contract changes would be needed.

hypotheses.statement: Missing or corrupted AMI register reads from the MDMS cause estimation substitution and billing errors, driving the dispute increase.
hypotheses.rationale: Loss of AMI data would require improving data ingestion or MDMS exports, not just an AI ticket responder.

hypotheses.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules have increased false rejections or mis-bills, raising dispute volume.
hypotheses.rationale: If rule changes are at fault, adjusting validation logic or rule management would be needed alongside any AI agent.
